title: Vectorial Boolean nonlinearity beyond the Nyberg threshold
summary: Determine the maximum component nonlinearity of maps from F2^n to F2^m when the output dimension exceeds the bent-function threshold.

formal_statement.body: For $n=2k$ and $k<m<n$, determine $\mathcal N(n,m)=\max_{F:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2^m}\min_{0\ne v\in\mathbb F_2^m}\operatorname{NL}(v\cdot F)$, where $\operatorname{NL}(h)=2^{n-1}-\tfrac12\max_a|W_h(a)|$ and $W_h$ is the Walsh transform.

scope.domain: Vectorial Boolean functions and component nonlinearity
scope.unresolved_remainder: Tightness of the general upper bound for all admissible (n,m) remains outside the public record.

citations.label: Wadayama et al., vectorial Boolean nonlinearity
Xu--Carlet--Mesnager--Wu, upper bounds in the range m > n/2

progress.summary: Nyberg's threshold rules out vectorial bentness once the output dimension exceeds the half-dimension threshold.
Coding-theoretic work formulates the optimization problem and records non-tight general bounds.
